1 preamble

As a proof of concept, we will process 10x Genomics Visium data comprising a single tissue section from a colorectal cancer biopsy (de Oliveira et al. 2025).

1.1 libs

library(miro)
library(scran)
library(scater)
library(ggplot2)
library(VisiumIO)
library(OSTA.data)
library(patchwork)
library(HDF5Array)
library(SpatialExperiment)
set.seed(260303)

1.2 data

We’ll start out by retrieving vendor outputs with OSTA.data`, reading data into a SpatialExperiment with VisiumIO, and performing minimal processing, namely: - log-library size normalization - identifying highly variable features - principal component analysis (PCA)

# retrieval
id <- "Visium_HumanColon_Oliveira"
pa <- OSTA.data_load(id)
dir.create(td <- tempfile())
unzip(pa, exdir=td)

# loading
spe <- TENxVisium(
    spacerangerOut=file.path(td, "outs"),
    images="lowres", format="h5") |>
    import()

# wrangling
metadata(spe) <- list()
rownames(spe) <- rowData(spe)$Symbol
img <- as.raster(imgData(spe)$data[[1]])
imgData(spe)$data[[1]] <- SpatialImage(img)

# processing
spe <- logNormCounts(spe)
tbl <- modelGeneVar(spe)
hvg <- getTopHVGs(tbl, n=2e3)
spe <- runPCA(spe, subset_row=hvg)
spe
## class: SpatialExperiment 
## dim: 18085 4269 
## metadata(0):
## assays(2): counts logcounts
## rownames(18085): SAMD11 NOC2L ... MT-ND6 MT-CYB
## rowData names(3): ID Symbol Type
## colnames(4269): AACAATGTGCTCCGAG-1 AACACCATTCGCATAC-1 ...
##   TGTTGGTGCGGAATCA-1 TGTTGGTGGACTCAGG-1
## colData names(5): in_tissue array_row array_col sample_id sizeFactor
## reducedDimNames(1): PCA
## mainExpName: Gene Expression
## altExpNames(0):
## spatialCoords names(2) : pxl_col_in_fullres pxl_row_in_fullres
## imgData names(4): sample_id image_id data scaleFactor

Let’s visualize the corresponding hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. On the right-hand side, we crop to the region covered by Visium spots:

mx <- as.raster(getImg(spe))
sf <- imgData(spe)$scaleFactor
xy <- sf*spatialCoords(spe)
xy <- ceiling(colRanges(xy))
i <- seq(xy[2, 1], xy[2, 2])
j <- seq(xy[1, 1], xy[1, 2])
plot(mx[rev(seq_len(nrow(mx))), ])
do.call(rect, as.list(c(xy)))
plot(mx[rev(i), j])

2 analysis

We can now interpret PCs in terms of colors by rescaling and interpreting them as coordinates in the CIELAB color space (see ?colorspace::LAB()), where

  • \(a\in[-100,100]\) green-red (\(<0\) = green, \(>0\) = red)
  • \(b\in[-100,100]\) blue-yellow (\(<0\) = blue, \(>0\) = yellow)
  • \(L\in[0,100]\) lightness or luminance (0 = black, 100 = white).

By default, PCs 1-3 will be used for ABL, but argument dims (default 3L) can be used to control which components to use.

head(df <- calcHex(spe))
##                           PC1       PC2         PC3
## AACAATGTGCTCCGAG-1 -43.628352  6.022533 -12.4218270
## AACACCATTCGCATAC-1  69.226179 -7.850156 -10.6582607
## AACACGACAACGGAGT-1 -41.817358  6.377981  -2.0958909
## AACACGCAGATAACAA-1  67.196489  3.663722  -0.4551566
## AACACGTTGATACCGC-1 -21.516673  6.799241   0.3458462
## AACACTCGTGAGCTTC-1   4.348308 23.611565  22.1842221
##                           L         A        B     hex
## AACAATGTGCTCCGAG-1 40.20300 -86.99613 53.45865 #007800
## AACACCATTCGCATAC-1 42.63989  85.30148 25.76869 #DD0040
## AACACGACAACGGAGT-1 54.47135 -84.23124 54.16812 #009F09
## AACACGCAGATAACAA-1 56.73852  82.20271 48.75045 #FF1739
## AACACGTTGATACCGC-1 57.84534 -53.23772 55.00896 #369F19
## AACACTCGTGAGCTTC-1 88.02157 -13.74906 88.56645 #EFE100
pc <- reducedDim(spe, "PCA")
ts <- c(0, -0.5*pi, -pi, -1.5*pi)
names(ts) <- c("0", "-pi/2", "-pi", "-3pi/2")
lapply(names(ts), \(.) {
    fd <- calcHex(spe, t=ts[.])
    df <- data.frame(pc, fd)
    ggplot(fd, aes(A, B, col=hex)) + 
    ggtitle(paste("theta =", .)) +
    ggplot(df, aes(PC1, PC2, col=hex)) +
    plot_layout(ncol=1) &
        geom_point(alpha=0.5) &
        scale_color_identity() &
        theme_bw() & coord_equal() &
        theme(panel.grid.minor=element_blank())
}) |> wrap_plots(nrow=1)

3.2 biplot

TODO: come up w better viz, e.g., circular with repeling labels?

We can also visualize feature loadings in a biplot with the LAB color space as background (note that \(L\) remains fixed here). Argument gs may be used to control which features to include; this can be either a character vector or scalar integer, in which case the top-gs features in each dimension will be determined (per absolute values).

ig <- grepv("^IGH", rownames(spe))
miroBiplot(spe, gs=5L) +
miroBiplot(spe, gs=ig, L=100)
